label: Bonus Class 3
title: Background and Action: Was Doing vs Did
titleAr: الخلفية والحدث: was doing مقابل did
bigIdea: A story has two layers: the background, filmed like a video (was/were + -ing: It was raining, people were waiting), and the events, taken like snapshots (past simple: the bus arrived). English chooses the form by how we look at the action, not only by when it happened.
bigIdeaAr: للقصة طبقتان: الخلفية، وتُصوَّر كفيديو (was/were + -ing: كانت تمطر، كان الناس ينتظرون)، والأحداث، وتُلتقط كصور سريعة (الماضي البسيط: وصل الباص). الإنجليزية تختار الصيغة حسب طريقة نظرنا إلى الفعل، لا حسب وقت حدوثه فقط.
builtOn: Bonus Class 2: the story mountain (setting = background)
Lesson 9: feelings in the past (nervous, relieved, proud, embarrassed, thrilled)
Lesson 10: past continuous intro (was studying, was raining, were waiting, storm, thunder, bus stop, umbrella, shelter)
Lessons 11-12: past simple review (reviewed, practiced, passed, packed, flew, arrived, explored, airport, suitcase, boarding pass, hotel)

objectives.en: I can explain the difference between background (was/were + -ing) and events (past simple) in a story.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أشرح الفرق بين الخلفية (was/were + -ing) والأحداث (الماضي البسيط) في القصة.

objectives.en: I can draw a timeline that shows a long action and a short action that interrupts it.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أرسم خطاً زمنياً يُظهر فعلاً طويلاً وفعلاً قصيراً يقطعه.

objectives.en: I can join two actions with when and while.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أربط فعلين باستخدام when و while.

objectives.en: I can translate كان + المضارع correctly: sometimes 'was doing', sometimes 'did' or 'used to do'.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أترجم «كان + المضارع» بشكل صحيح: أحياناً was doing وأحياناً did أو used to do.

keyTerms.meaning: Where an action sits in time. English verbs show past or present: walked, walk.
How we look at an action: as a complete dot (did) or from inside, in progress (was doing).
What was happening around the story: the weather, the scene, long actions.
The short, complete actions that move the story forward.
A line that shows the order and length of actions.
To stop or break into a longer action: The phone rang while I was studying.

facts.en: Linguists separate two ideas in a verb. Tense says WHEN (past or present). Aspect says HOW we look at the action: from outside as one complete dot, or from inside while it is still going on.
facts.ar: يفرّق اللغويون بين فكرتين في الفعل: الزمن يقول «متى» (ماضٍ أو حاضر)، والجهة تقول «كيف ننظر إلى الفعل»: من الخارج كنقطة كاملة، أو من الداخل وهو ما زال مستمراً.

facts.en: Past simple = a snapshot: the action is complete (The bus arrived). Past continuous = a video: we are inside the action, it has no start or end on screen (It was raining).
facts.ar: الماضي البسيط = صورة فوتوغرافية: الفعل كامل (وصل الباص). الماضي المستمر = فيديو: نحن داخل الفعل، ولا نرى بدايته ولا نهايته (كانت تمطر).

facts.en: Linguists who study stories in many languages (for example Paul Hopper, in 1979) noticed the same thing in language after language: storytellers separate the foreground (the main events, in order) from the background (the scene, the reasons, what was going on). Languages just use different tools to do it.
facts.ar: لاحظ لغويون درسوا القصص في لغات كثيرة (مثل بول هوبر) الأمر نفسه في لغة بعد أخرى: الراوي يفصل بين المقدّمة (الأحداث الرئيسية بالترتيب) والخلفية (المشهد والأسباب وما كان يجري). اللغات تستخدم أدوات مختلفة فقط.

facts.en: The same two actions can tell two different stories: 'When Sara arrived, we ate' (she came, THEN we ate). 'When Sara arrived, we were eating' (we started BEFORE she came). One small -ing changes the timeline.
facts.ar: الفعلان نفساهما قد يحكيان قصتين مختلفتين: When Sara arrived, we ate (جاءت ثم أكلنا). When Sara arrived, we were eating (بدأنا قبل وصولها). حرف -ing صغير يغيّر الخط الزمني.

facts.en: Some verbs do not like the video camera. State verbs (know, like, want, need, believe) describe a situation, not an activity, so we usually say 'I knew', not 'I was knowing'.
facts.ar: بعض الأفعال لا تحب كاميرا الفيديو. أفعال الحالة (know, like, want, need, believe) تصف وضعاً لا نشاطاً، لذلك نقول عادة I knew وليس I was knowing.

facts.en: Many linguists say Arabic ماضٍ and مضارع are also partly about aspect: ماضٍ often means a complete action, and مضارع an incomplete or ongoing one. That is why كان + مضارع (كان يلعب) can paint an action in progress in the past.
facts.ar: يرى كثير من اللغويين أن الماضي والمضارع في العربية يتعلقان جزئياً بالجهة أيضاً: الماضي غالباً حدث مكتمل، والمضارع حدث غير مكتمل أو مستمر. ولهذا يرسم «كان + المضارع» (كان يلعب) فعلاً مستمراً في الماضي.

arabicBridge.english: He was playing football when it started to rain.
arabicBridge.arabic: كان يلعب كرة القدم عندما بدأ المطر.
arabicBridge.point: A great match: كان + المضارع ≈ was/were + -ing for an action in progress. Both need TWO pieces: كان + يلعب, was + playing.
arabicBridge.pointAr: تطابق رائع: كان + المضارع ≈ was/were + -ing لفعل مستمر في الماضي. وكلاهما يحتاج قطعتين: كان + يلعب، was + playing.

arabicBridge.english: He played football every Friday. / He used to play football every Friday.
arabicBridge.arabic: كان يلعب كرة القدم كل يوم جمعة.
arabicBridge.point: Careful! The same Arabic form can also mean a past HABIT (something that happened again and again). For a past habit English usually does NOT use was playing; it uses the past simple or used to.
arabicBridge.pointAr: انتبه! الصيغة العربية نفسها قد تعني أيضاً عادة متكررة في الماضي. وللعادة في الماضي لا تستخدم الإنجليزية عادةً was playing، بل الماضي البسيط أو used to.

arabicBridge.point: while usually goes with the long background action (while I was studying); when usually goes with the short event (when the phone rang). Arabic بينما and عندما work in a similar way.
arabicBridge.pointAr: while تأتي عادة مع الفعل الطويل في الخلفية (while I was studying)، و when مع الحدث القصير (when the phone rang). وتعمل «بينما» و«عندما» بطريقة مشابهة.

arabicBridge.point: English has no single ending for 'in progress'; it builds it from be + -ing. Arabic speakers sometimes keep only one piece: 'I was study' or 'I studying'. Both pieces are needed.
arabicBridge.pointAr: لا توجد في الإنجليزية نهاية واحدة للاستمرار، بل تُبنى من be + -ing. وأحياناً يكتفي متحدثو العربية بقطعة واحدة: I was study أو I studying. القطعتان ضروريتان.

commonErrors.wrong: When I watched TV, the phone rang. (meaning: I was in the middle of watching)
commonErrors.right: When I was watching TV, the phone rang. / While I was watching TV, the phone rang.
commonErrors.why: Using the snapshot (past simple) for the background. 'When I watched TV, the phone rang' sounds like two short events, one after the other.

commonErrors.wrong: I was study when the lights went out.
commonErrors.right: I was studying when the lights went out.
commonErrors.why: Translating كنت أدرس piece by piece and forgetting -ing.

commonErrors.wrong: They waiting at the bus stop.
commonErrors.right: They were waiting at the bus stop.
commonErrors.why: Forgetting was/were: Arabic كانوا ينتظرون has two pieces, but students sometimes keep only the -ing.

commonErrors.wrong: When I was a child, I was playing football every day.
commonErrors.right: When I was a child, I played (used to play) football every day.
commonErrors.why: كان يلعب كل يوم is a habit; English uses past simple or used to, not past continuous.
know, like, want, need are state verbs and usually do not take -ing.

commonErrors.wrong: While the phone rang, I was sleeping.
commonErrors.right: When the phone rang, I was sleeping. / While I was sleeping, the phone rang.
commonErrors.why: while goes with the long action, when with the short one.

teacher: A storm-at-the-bus-stop picture (Lesson 10) and an airport picture (Lesson 12)
Two camera icons: Video camera (background) and Photo camera (event)
Timeline template on the Teams Whiteboard
Short story 'The Airport Day' on a slide
student: Two cards: a video camera and a photo camera (or the letters B and E)

stages.name: Warm-up: Freeze Frame
stages.purpose: Revive was/were + -ing from Lesson 10 and feel the 'video' meaning before naming it.
teacherSays: Look at the picture: a storm, a bus stop. I press PAUSE. What was happening at that moment? It was raining. People were waiting...
Now your life: what were you doing yesterday at 8 o'clock in the evening? And at 7 this morning?
Ziad says: 'At 8 pm I was studying for my exam. Suddenly, the lights went out!' Two kinds of verbs. Can you hear them?
teacherSaysAr: أوقفت الصورة. ماذا كان يحدث في تلك اللحظة؟
ماذا كنت تفعل أمس الساعة الثامنة مساءً؟
studentsDo: Describe the frozen picture with was/were + -ing (3-4 sentences together).
Answer 'What were you doing at...?' about their own day.
tips: Accept short answers; the goal is to warm up the form.
Write Ziad's two sentences on the slide; they are the anchor for Stage 2.

stages.name: Linguistics Corner: The Video Camera and the Photo Camera
stages.nameAr: ركن اللغويات: كاميرا الفيديو وكاميرا الصور
stages.method: Guided discovery with a visual metaphor (concept checking questions)
stages.purpose: Discover tense vs aspect and the background/foreground roles in a story.
teacherSays: Every storyteller has two cameras. The video camera films the background: it was raining, people were waiting. We are INSIDE the action. We don't see the start or the end.
The photo camera takes snapshots: the bus arrived, the lights went out. Click! Complete actions. They move the story forward.
Linguists have names for this. Tense = when: past. Aspect = how we look at it: from inside (was doing) or as a complete dot (did).
Concept check: 'It was raining.' Did the rain stop in this sentence? We don't know! 'It rained.' Is it complete? Yes.
Now read 'The Airport Day'. For each sentence, hold up your video camera or your photo camera.
teacherSaysAr: للراوي كاميرتان: كاميرا الفيديو تصوّر الخلفية ونحن داخل الحدث، وكاميرا الصور تلتقط أحداثاً كاملة تحرّك القصة.
الزمن = متى. الجهة = كيف ننظر إلى الحدث.
studentsDo: Listen to the two-camera explanation and answer the concept questions.
Read 'The Airport Day' and show the video (B) or photo (E) card for each sentence.
Find the pattern: which verb form is in every B sentence?

exercise.instructions: Is it background (B, video camera) or event (E, photo camera)?
exercise.instructionsAr: هل هي خلفية (B، كاميرا الفيديو) أم حدث (E، كاميرا الصور)؟

items.prompt: It was a hot morning, and hundreds of people were waiting at the airport.
items.answer: B

items.prompt: Sara and her family were standing in a long queue.
items.answer: B

items.prompt: Her little brother was playing a game on his phone.
items.answer: B

items.prompt: Suddenly, Sara checked her bag.
items.answer: E

items.prompt: She shouted, 'Where is my boarding pass?'
items.answer: E

items.prompt: She ran back to the café.
items.answer: E

items.prompt: A waiter was cleaning the tables and holding a small piece of paper.
items.answer: B

items.prompt: He smiled and gave her the boarding pass. Sara felt so relieved!
items.answer: E

tips: Sentence 1 has 'It was a hot morning' (a state with was) and 'were waiting': both set the scene. The test is the sentence's job in the story: does it set the scene (B) or move the story forward (E)?
Draw the two camera icons on every later slide of the class.

stages.name: Timeline Lab: Long Lines and Lightning
stages.nameAr: مختبر الخط الزمني: خطوط طويلة وبرق
stages.purpose: See the shape of each form on a timeline and understand how one -ing changes the meaning.
teacherSays: Draw a line: past on the left, now on the right. The background is a long wavy line: ~~~~~ I was studying. The event is a lightning bolt across it: the lights went out!
Now two actions in snapshots: When the bus arrived, we got on. Two dots: first the bus, then us.
Detective time! 'When Sara arrived, we ate.' 'When Sara arrived, we were eating.' Draw both. Who started eating first?
One -ing can change the whole story!
teacherSaysAr: الخلفية خط طويل متموّج، والحدث برق يقطعه.
When Sara arrived, we ate = وصلت ثم أكلنا. When Sara arrived, we were eating = كنا نأكل قبل وصولها.
studentsDo: Draw timelines for 3 sentences on paper and show them to the camera.
Answer each meaning question in the exercise.
Make one pair of their own: 'When Dad came home, I ___ / was ___ing.'

exercise.instructions: Read the sentence and answer the question about the timeline.
exercise.instructionsAr: اقرأ الجملة وأجب عن سؤال الخط الزمني.

items.prompt: When Sara arrived, we ate. Did we start eating before or after she arrived?
items.answer: after

items.prompt: When Sara arrived, we were eating. Did we start eating before or after she arrived?
items.answer: before

items.prompt: When the storm started, Omar ran to the shelter. Was Omar already running when the storm started?
items.answer: no (he started running after the storm started)

items.prompt: When the storm started, Omar was running to the shelter. Was Omar already running?
items.answer: yes

items.prompt: I was reviewing my notes when the teacher came in. Which action is longer?
items.answer: reviewing my notes

items.prompt: While we were exploring the old town, it started to rain. Which action interrupts?
items.answer: it started to rain

items.prompt: We packed our suitcases. Then we flew to Cairo. Background or a list of events?
items.answer: a list of events (past simple, in order)

tips: Make students draw, not just answer: the drawing is the memory.
The pairs in items 1-4 are the heart of the class; spend time there.

stages.name: Arabic Bridge: كان يلعب — Video or Habit?
stages.nameAr: جسر العربية: «كان يلعب» فيديو أم عادة؟
stages.purpose: Use the strong match كان + المضارع ≈ was/were + -ing for one moment in progress, and avoid the habit trap.
teacherSays: Good news first: Arabic already has a video camera! كان يلعب (at one moment) = he was playing. كنت أدرس = I was studying. Two pieces in Arabic, two pieces in English.

Now a trap. 'كان يلعب كرة القدم كل يوم جمعة.' Is that one long action at one moment? No! It is a habit, many Fridays. English says: He played football every Friday, or He used to play football every Friday.
So before you translate كان + مضارع, ask: is it one moment in progress, or a habit? Moment = was playing. Habit = played / used to play.
And بينما? Usually while. عندما? when.
teacherSaysAr: العربية لديها كاميرا فيديو أيضاً: كان يلعب = was playing.
لكن «كان يلعب كل جمعة» عادة، وليست لحظة مستمرة؛ فنقول played أو used to play.
اسأل نفسك: لحظة مستمرة أم عادة؟
studentsDo: Decide 'moment' or 'habit' for each Arabic sentence, then translate it.
Explain one decision to the group.
Make one Arabic sentence of their own for a partner to translate.

exercise.instructions: Moment or habit? Translate into English.
exercise.instructionsAr: لحظة أم عادة؟ ترجم إلى الإنجليزية.

items.prompt: كنت أدرس عندما انقطعت الكهرباء.
items.answer: Moment: I was studying when the lights (power) went out.

items.prompt: كان جدي يزورنا كل أسبوع.
items.answer: Habit: My grandpa visited us (used to visit us) every week.

items.prompt: كانت تمطر عندما وصلنا إلى الفندق.
items.answer: Moment: It was raining when we arrived at the hotel.

items.prompt: بينما كان عمر ينتظر الباص، رأى صديقه.
items.answer: Moment: While Omar was waiting for the bus, he saw his friend.

items.prompt: كانت نور تتمرّن على البيانو كل يوم عندما كانت صغيرة.
items.answer: Habit: Noor practiced (used to practice) the piano every day when she was little.

items.prompt: كانوا يتحدثون عندما دخل المعلم.
items.answer: Moment: They were talking when the teacher came in.

tips: For past habits, 'would' is also correct (My grandpa would visit us every week); accept it from strong students. Was + -ing for a habit is natural only in special cases (a short, temporary period, or a complaint with 'always'); keep the rule simple for this age.
Praise the Arabic knowledge: students who understand كان + مضارع already understand the past continuous.

stages.name: Team Game: Interrupted!
stages.method: Sentence combining race (gamified practice) with when / while
stages.purpose: Build accurate complex sentences with when and while, choosing the right form for each action.
teacherSays: Two teams. I give you two actions: one long, one short. Join them with when or while. Correct sentence = 1 point. Correct in TWO ways (with when AND with while) = 2 points!
Example: I / sleep (long) + the thunder / wake me up (short). When: 'I was sleeping when the thunder woke me up.' While: 'While I was sleeping, the thunder woke me up.'
Ready? Interrupted!
teacherSaysAr: أعطيكم فعلين: طويلاً وقصيراً. اربطوهما بـ when أو while. جملة صحيحة = نقطة، وبطريقتين = نقطتان!
studentsDo: Combine the two actions orally, then type the sentence in the chat.
Try for the double-point version with both when and while.
Check the other team's sentence: is the long action in was/were + -ing?

exercise.instructions: Join the long action and the short action with when or while.
exercise.instructionsAr: اربط الفعل الطويل بالفعل القصير باستخدام when أو while.

items.prompt: we / wait at the bus stop + the storm / start
items.answer: We were waiting at the bus stop when the storm started. / While we were waiting at the bus stop, the storm started.

items.prompt: Hamad / pack his suitcase + his phone / ring
items.answer: Hamad was packing his suitcase when his phone rang. / While Hamad was packing his suitcase, his phone rang.

items.prompt: I / review my notes + I / find an old photo
items.answer: I was reviewing my notes when I found an old photo. / While I was reviewing my notes, I found an old photo.

items.prompt: they / explore the landmark + they / meet a famous actor
items.answer: They were exploring the landmark when they met a famous actor. / While they were exploring the landmark, they met a famous actor.

items.prompt: Mom / cook dinner + the lights / go out
items.answer: Mom was cooking dinner when the lights went out. / While Mom was cooking dinner, the lights went out.

items.prompt: Noor / walk to class + she / drop her umbrella
items.answer: Noor was walking to class when she dropped her umbrella. / While Noor was walking to class, she dropped her umbrella.

items.prompt: we / fly to Dubai + the pilot / make an announcement
items.answer: We were flying to Dubai when the pilot made an announcement. / While we were flying to Dubai, the pilot made an announcement.

items.prompt: Ziad / study for the exam + his friends / call him
items.answer: Ziad was studying for the exam when his friends called him. / While Ziad was studying..., his friends called him.

tips: Accept both orders; point out the comma when the while/when part comes first.
If a team writes 'was rang', ask: is ringing long or short? Snapshot verbs stay simple.

stages.name: Error Clinic: Wrong Camera!
stages.purpose: Repair the typical errors: past simple for background, missing pieces, habits and state verbs.
teacherSays: These sentences used the wrong camera, or lost a piece! Fix each one and say 'wrong camera', 'missing piece' or 'state verb'.
teacherSaysAr: هذه الجمل استخدمت الكاميرا الخاطئة أو فقدت قطعة! أصلح كل جملة واذكر السبب.
studentsDo: Correct the sentences in pairs.
Name the reason for each correction.

exercise.instructions: Correct the sentence and name the problem.

items.prompt: When I watched TV, the phone rang. (I was in the middle of a movie.)
items.answer: When I was watching TV, the phone rang. (wrong camera: background needs -ing)

items.prompt: I was study when the lights went out.
items.answer: I was studying... (missing piece: -ing)

items.prompt: They waiting at the airport when we arrived.
items.answer: They were waiting... (missing piece: were)

items.prompt: When I was ten, I was going to the beach every weekend.
items.answer: I went / used to go to the beach every weekend. (habit, not a moment)

items.prompt: I was knowing the answer, but I was nervous.
items.answer: I knew the answer... (state verb)

items.prompt: While the bus arrived, we were talking.
items.answer: When the bus arrived, we were talking. / While we were talking, the bus arrived. (while + long action)

tips: Keep it quick; the reason words become class language for later lessons.
Lesson 16 reviews 'while' with two long actions; this is the foundation.

stages.name: Director's Cut: Set the Scene, Then Action!
stages.nameAr: نسخة المخرج: اصنع المشهد ثم... أكشن!
stages.method: Creative writing in role (film director) + peer feedback
stages.purpose: Write a story opening with a background layer, a feeling, and an event that breaks in.
teacherSays: You are film directors. Choose a scene. First, the video camera: two background sentences (weather, people, what was happening). Then a feeling: I was nervous / thrilled. Then... ACTION! One event with 'suddenly' or 'when'.
Example: 'It was raining hard. People were running to the shelter. I was waiting for the bus and I was very calm. Suddenly, there was a huge clap of thunder and...'
Read your scene with a director's voice. Listeners: say which sentence was the video and which was the click.
teacherSaysAr: أنتم مخرجون: جملتان للخلفية بكاميرا الفيديو، ثم شعور، ثم حدث مفاجئ مع suddenly أو when.
studentsDo: Choose one scene card and write 4-5 sentences (background, feeling, event).
Read the scene aloud dramatically.
Peer feedback: find the video sentences and the click sentence; give one star and one wish.

exercise.instructions: Choose a scene. Write 2 background sentences, 1 feeling, 1 event.
exercise.instructionsAr: اختر مشهداً. اكتب جملتين للخلفية وشعوراً واحداً وحدثاً واحداً.

items.prompt: Scene 1: the bus stop in a storm
items.answer: Model: It was raining and the wind was blowing. Three people were waiting under one umbrella. I was cold but calm. Suddenly, a car stopped and my uncle opened the door!

items.prompt: Scene 2: the exam room
items.answer: Model: It was very quiet. Everybody was writing. I was nervous. When I turned the page, I saw a question I knew!

items.prompt: Scene 3: the airport
items.answer: Model: The airport was crowded. Families were pushing big suitcases. I was thrilled. Suddenly, they called my name!

items.prompt: Scene 4: the hotel at night
items.answer: Model: It was midnight. My brother was sleeping and I was reading. Suddenly, someone knocked on the door.

items.prompt: Scene 5: the school trip to a landmark
items.answer: Model: The sun was shining. Our teacher was explaining the history of the old castle. I was looking at the old walls when I saw a small door.

items.prompt: Scene 6: the football match
items.answer: Model: Thousands of fans were singing. We were losing 1-0. I was disappointed. Then, in the last minute, Omar scored!

tips: Models are examples only; any scene with correct background and event forms is right.
Ask students to save their scenes: Bonus Class 4 turns them into dramatic readings.

stages.name: Exit Ticket, Did You Know? and Goodbye
stages.purpose: Check form, meaning and the Arabic trap individually.
teacherSays: Exit ticket: five questions in the chat.

Did you know? Film scripts use the same two layers! A script describes the scene first ('Rain is falling. People are waiting.') and then the action. Storytelling and film-making share one grammar of attention.
Next class: we learn to SAY our stories like real storytellers. Bring your scene!
teacherSaysAr: هل تعلم؟ نصوص الأفلام تستخدم الطبقتين نفسيهما: وصف المشهد أولاً ثم الحدث.
studentsDo: Answer the 5 exit-ticket items.
Say goodbye with 'Yesterday at this time I was...'
tips: Students under 4/5 need more timeline drawing in the Lesson 13-16 warm-ups.

items.prompt: Complete: I ___ (sleep) when the thunder started.
items.answer: was sleeping

items.prompt: Complete: While we were waiting for the bus, it ___ (start) to rain.
items.answer: started

items.prompt: 'When Dad arrived, we were eating.' Did we start eating before or after he arrived?
items.answer: before

items.prompt: Translate: كان يلعب التنس كل صباح.
items.answer: He played (used to play) tennis every morning. (habit)

items.prompt: Correct it: I was knowing his name.
items.answer: I knew his name.

homework.en: Two-Layer Story: write the opening of a story (80-100 words) about a trip or a stormy day. Use at least three was/were + -ing sentences for the background, one feeling from Lesson 9, and three events in the past simple with when, while and suddenly. Draw the timeline under your story.
homework.ar: قصة الطبقتين: اكتب بداية قصة (80-100 كلمة) عن رحلة أو يوم عاصف. استخدم ثلاث جمل على الأقل بـ was/were + -ing للخلفية، وشعوراً واحداً من الدرس 9، وثلاثة أحداث بالماضي البسيط مع when و while و suddenly. ارسم الخط الزمني تحت قصتك.
tasks: Write the two-layer story opening (80-100 words).
Underline background verbs in one color and event verbs in another.
Draw the timeline with wavy lines and lightning bolts.

support: Give the two-camera cards with the forms printed on them: video = was/were + -ing; photo = -ed / fossil.
In the Interrupted! game, mark which action is long before students combine.
Let the student say the story in Arabic first, then choose the camera for each verb.
challenge: Use two background actions at the same time: While Mom was cooking, Dad was cleaning the car.
Write the same mini-story twice, once with 'we ate' and once with 'we were eating', and explain how the story changes.
Find a past continuous sentence in a song, movie or book and explain its job.

successCriteria: Classifies at least 6 of 8 story sentences as background or event.
Answers the meaning pairs (we ate / we were eating) correctly and draws the timelines.
Combines at least 6 of 8 action pairs correctly with when / while.
Translates كان + المضارع correctly as moment or habit in at least 4 of 6 items.
watchFor: Past simple for background ('When I watched TV, the phone rang')

teacherNotes: The core message is meaning, not form: the form was taught in Lesson 10. Keep asking 'video or photo?'.
The habit trap (كان يلعب كل يوم) is the most important Arabic point of the class; give it time.
Be modest about the Arabic aspect claim: 'many linguists describe it this way' is accurate; 'Arabic has no tense' is not.
Bonus Class 4 uses the scenes written today for dramatic reading with stress and rhythm.

deck.title: Foreground and background
deck.text: Linguists who study stories in many languages (for example Paul Hopper, 1979) noticed the same thing: storytellers separate the main events from the background. Languages just use different tools.
deck.ar: لاحظ اللغويون في لغات كثيرة أن الراوي يفصل بين الأحداث الرئيسية والخلفية، لكن كل لغة تستخدم أدوات مختلفة.

deck.title: Films use two layers too
deck.text: A film script describes the scene first ('Rain is falling. People are waiting.') and then the action. Storytelling and film-making share one grammar of attention.

items.q: 'It was raining' describes the background, like a video.
items.qAr: الجملة It was raining تصف الخلفية مثل الفيديو.

items.q: 'When Sara arrived, we were eating' means we started eating after she arrived.
items.qAr: معنى When Sara arrived, we were eating أننا بدأنا الأكل بعد وصولها.
items.why: We started before she arrived: the eating was already in progress.

items.q: 'I was knowing the answer' is correct English.
items.qAr: الجملة I was knowing the answer صحيحة.
items.why: know is a state verb: I knew the answer.

items.q: 'كان يلعب كل يوم جمعة' is a habit, so English says 'He played (used to play) every Friday'.
items.qAr: «كان يلعب كل يوم جمعة» عادة، فنقول بالإنجليزية He played (used to play) every Friday.

items.q: while usually goes with the long action.
items.qAr: تأتي while عادةً مع الفعل الطويل.

items.q: 'When I watched TV, the phone rang' shows I was in the middle of watching.
items.qAr: الجملة When I watched TV, the phone rang تعني أنني كنت في منتصف المشاهدة.
items.why: For an action in progress, say: When I was watching TV, the phone rang.

items.q: The past continuous needs two pieces: was / were + -ing.
